geometry_edits.rationale: Wrap the existing courtyard bar in a section-defining macro so the silhouette can move beyond a plain box while preserving the dominant gesture and public void.
Use a stable ridge family to introduce a calm but legible roof/section compatible with neighborhood living and the reference set.
Align the section profile along the long axis so the roof reads as one coherent continuous mass rather than isolated surface pieces.

graph_edits.rationale: Replace the simple lifted translate ending with a section-authoring operation so the form gains clearer upper hierarchy and a more legible neighborhood section.
Keep the lifted-ground effect minimal while the structural correction focuses on section rather than floating the whole mass higher.

rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent compact bar with a carved central void, and it maintains a legible dominant mass across all four views, so it clears the basic hard gates. The access edge response is acceptable because the main subtraction produces an open court/slot rather than a sealed frontage. The main weakness is that the silhouette is too much a generic rectangular extrusion with a narrow slot-like void; the stepped/sectional interest is limited and not yet strongly tied to neighborhood-living in an active-ground way. It resembles the reference family of courtyard bars and terraced community buildings, but it is still more box-driven than the strongest precedents. Program fit is plausible: a compact street building with one public void and calm upper massing is visible, though the section is not yet especially expressive.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Three-part composition with a central void and bridge-like upper connection can support a neighborhood/public ground relation.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much larger campus/tower composition; not directly transferable as a compact street building.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced courtyard-campus organization suggests how multiple masses can frame shared public space.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More transparent and landscape-driven than the opaque candidate mass.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Strong horizontal bar, central void, and curved/site-responsive plan offer a useful model for active-gound neighborhood massing.
Terraced ribbon sections and bridging circulation translate well to a compact mixed neighborhood building with public open space.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Larger multi-wing composition; candidate should stay more compact and less fragmented.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Interlocking volumes and a large central courtyard with setbacks are directly relevant to an active mixed-use threshold.

warnings: Dominant gesture is coherent, but the mass still skews box-like and under-articulated in section.
Void is legible, but its publicness could be stronger and more spatially generous.
The top/section remains fairly flat; if the intent is a more distinctive neighborhood landmark, a profiled or terraced roof/section could help.
